title: Decorator-Driven Validation Gaps
platform_conditions: Experimental decorators and emitDecoratorMetadata are compile-time transforms; validation only runs if the framework reads that metadata at runtime
security_mechanism: Validation declared purely as decorators (@ValidateRole) is inert data attached to the class: it executes only if the runtime actually loads reflect-metadata, imports the decorator's registering module, and invokes a validation pipeline over the metadata. Omit any of those -- enableMetadata off, tree-shaken side-effect import, no validation bootstrap -- and the compiled handler accepts anything while the source still reads as if a check exists. Missing metadata also fails silently: the validator sees no rules and returns 'valid' rather than erroring.

source_sink_clues.source: Request bodies and DTOs bound to decorator-annotated classes whose declared rules never execute at runtime.
source_sink_clues.sink: Validation/authorization decorators on properties or handlers that are trusted as enforced without verifying a runtime pipeline consumes them

tracking_guards: Check a runtime validator is bootstrapped (metadata reflect polyfill imported, validation middleware invoked per request) and fails closed; check a test or integration point asserts invalid payloads are actually rejected.
not_candidate_when: A test in the same tree demonstrates invalid input is rejected at runtime, validation runs in explicit middleware independent of decorator metadata, or the annotation is documentation-only on an internal type with no external entry point.
public_references: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
